headline: Kai, the Fed's first hike since 2023 is on the books, and futures spent the night deciding they can live with it.
subline: A quarter point to 3.75–4.00 percent with more signaled, Wednesday's 631-point Dow drop meeting firmer futures, and Brent easing as the Saudis patch their pipeline.
asof: Pre-market · as of 6:50 AM ET · index rows show Wednesday's close, S&P futures +0.7% pre-dawn; gold, Brent and bitcoin are morning quotes · every figure links to its source below

items.title: First hike since 2023: a quarter point, more signaled
items.sentence: The Fed raised its target range a quarter point Wednesday to 3.75–4.00 percent — its first increase since 2023 — and chair Kevin Warsh said inflation is still too high, per CNBC.

items.title: Futures firm into claims, housing starts and the BoE
items.sentence: S&P 500 futures rose 0.7 percent overnight as Warsh's hawkish tone read as resolve on inflation rather than alarm, with jobless claims, August housing starts and a Bank of England decision still ahead today, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Wednesday's bill: Dow off 631, S&P down 0.45
items.sentence: Wednesday's damage landed mostly on blue chips — the Dow fell 631 points to 51,461.90 and the S&P 500 lost 0.45 percent to 7,551.81, while the Nasdaq closed essentially flat, per The Motley Fool.

items.title: Gold reclaims $4,300 as an inflation input cools
items.sentence: Gold rose 1.03 percent to $4,307.57 this morning, back above $4,300 as easing oil prices took some pressure off the inflation picture, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Brent eases as Saudi pipeline repairs advance
items.sentence: Brent slipped 1.17 percent to $104.59, a second straight decline, after reports that Saudi Arabia will restore roughly half of the East-West pipeline's capacity within days, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Bitcoin takes the hike near $76,000
items.sentence: Bitcoin trades at $76,025 this morning, down 1.24 percent over 24 hours — a contained move through the first Fed hike since 2023, per Forbes Advisor.

items.title: Trump: Iran war 'toward the end,' spoke with Tehran
items.sentence: Trump said the war with Iran is 'toward the end' and claimed he has spoken directly with Tehran, the clearest de-escalation talk as the conflict passes day 201, per Al Jazeera's live coverage.

items.title: Seven quiet days; 103 ships turned from Hormuz
items.sentence: Iran has gone seven days without striking a regional state — its longest pause since August 28 — while CENTCOM's Hormuz blockade tally reached 103 redirected commercial vessels, per GlobalSecurity's daily report.

items.title: EU invites Canada to be first 'associate member'
items.sentence: The EU invited Canada to become its first 'associate member,' a novel arrangement Brussels rolled out as Trump's tariffs push Ottawa toward Europe, per NPR.

items.title: Coalition downs Houthi drone headed for Mecca
items.sentence: A Saudi-led coalition intercepted a Houthi drone headed for Mecca, the first attempted strike on the holy city since July 2017, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: WHO: DR Congo Ebola fight 'far from over'
items.sentence: The WHO chief warned that the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo is 'far from over,' a reminder the year's other emergencies continue outside the war headlines, per Al Jazeera.

items.title: Amazon hands Generac an $8 billion power order
items.sentence: Generac surged 40 percent after hours on an Amazon deal worth up to $8 billion for backup generators at AI data centers — the power bottleneck, now with a price tag, per Stocktwits.

items.title: Huawei sets 2027 chips squarely at Nvidia
items.sentence: Huawei will launch two new AI chips in 2027, an explicit run at Nvidia's dominance in training silicon, per Reuters.

items.title: Snap ships $2,195 Specs with built-in assistant
items.sentence: Snap launched its $2,195 Specs AR glasses, pairing the hardware with an on-device assistant it calls Specs Intelligence, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Nebius raises GPU prices again; stock jumps
items.sentence: Nebius announced a second price increase for on-demand Nvidia GPU compute effective October 1, sending the stock up 8 percent in early trading, per Stocktwits.

items.title: Gemini 3.8 speaks while it reasons
items.sentence: Google released Gemini 3.8 voice models that talk while reasoning through tasks and running tools, scoring 82.6 on Artificial Analysis' speech-to-speech index, per AI Weekly's daily brief.
